FOREWORD

Indian Standard, which is identical with IS0 3407 : 1983 `Information processing Information interchange on 3.81 mm ( 0.150 in ) magnetic tape cassette at 4 cpmm ( 100 cpi ), phase encoded at 63 ftpmm ( 1 600 ftpi )`. issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards. on 15 December 1989 on the recommendation of the Computers, Business Machines and Calculators Sectional Committee ( LTDC 24 ) and approval of the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. In the adopted standard certain terminology and conventions are not identical Indian Standards; attention is specially drawn to the following. be read as #Indian Standard'. with those used in

a) Wherever the words `international Standard' appear, referring to this standard, they should b) Comma ( , ) has been used as a decimal marker while in Indian Standards the current
practice is to use point ( . ) as the decimal marker.

d

For the purpose of Indian Standard, metric dimensions are applicable.

8.3.2

The recording

starts with track No. 1; at its conclusion

the cassette may be turned over and the recording can be continued with track No. 2.

7.6

Number

of elongated

gaps 8.4 Use of tracks
(see 8.11.4) The use of track No. 1 is reserved for data interchange. The use of track No. 2 is to be indicated on the label. If it is not used in the same way as track No. 1, reading agreement between of track No. 2 requires sender and recipient of the cassette.

The number

of gaps which

have been elongated

due to erase instructions is a matter of agreement between interchange parties, but it is recommended that this number does not exceed 2, or alternatively 1 % of the total number of blocks written, whichever figure is larger.

Annex Layer-to-layer

A adhesion

(This annex forms part of the standard.)

The procedure for testing the tape for layer-to-layer adhesion is as follows: A piece of the tape to be tested, about 1 m (39 in) in length, shall be wound around a glass pipe, 36 mm (1.4 in) in diameter, with a tension of 3 N (0.67 Ibf), and fixed at the end. This shall be stored for 24 h at a temperature of 45 f 3 OC (113 f 6 OF) and at 60 % rela#ive humidity. After this period it shall be stored for another 24 h in the testing environment specified in clause 4. The tape shall then be unwound with a mass of 5 g at the end of the tape as shown in figure 7, and the angle 0 shall be smaller than 45O.

Figure 7 -

Test for layer-to-layer

adhesion

B.2.5

Measuring

equipment

The measuring equipment should be connected directly across the photoelectric cell to measure the outout current. In order to be able to set measuring equipment to full scale deflection (100 %I a shunt potentiometer in the circuit shall be provided or a fine adjustment of the lamp power supply voltage is required. The load impedance across the photoelectric cell should be as low as possible and shall not exceed 500 a. The instrument, which could take the form of a moving coil meter with a full scale deflection of 50 VA, should be capable of measuring values to an accuracy of IL 1 %. the maximum and minimum
